briefing:
The headline Airfare Price Index (APIx) advanced to 101.35, recording a modest day-on-base inflation of 1.35 percent across the monitored domestic trunk corridors. This movement reflects a broader trend of steady, moderate upward pressure on domestic passenger airfares, driven primarily by intermediate booking windows as passenger demand consolidates in the one-to-four-week pre-departure horizon. Despite isolated pockets of deflationary discounting in extended advance windows and selective last-minute price relaxation, overall airfare yields exhibit a firming trajectory, maintaining a mild positive contribution to the transport services component of consumer price inflation.

At the route level, market expansion was principally anchored by the Delhi–Bengaluru corridor, which posted a route APIx of 104.11 (a 4.11 percent increase over the base period). This upward push was predominantly driven by significant price escalation in the intermediate booking windows, notably T+30 (price relativity of 110.15) and T+7 (price relativity of 107.86). The market’s largest route by weight, Delhi–Bombay (40 percent system weight), demonstrated high price stability, edging up slightly with an APIx of 100.83 (+0.83 percent). Conversely, the Calcutta–Bombay corridor acted as a partial deflationary counterweight with a route APIx of 99.28 (-0.72 percent), weighed down significantly by a steep drop in long-horizon pricing despite strong upward pressure in its T+30 (109.46) and T+7 (105.13) windows.

A critical analytical finding involves the granular target day dataset, which triggered a pipeline error flag indicating raw scraped flight-level logs were missing for micro-validation. Nevertheless, aggregate median abstractions reveal significant pricing anomalies. Most prominent is the severe structural drop in Calcutta–Bombay’s T+45 booking window, where median fares plummeted 25.78 percent from baseline levels of ₹12,915 to ₹9,585. Furthermore, both the Delhi–Bengaluru and Calcutta–Bombay routes displayed non-standard yield curve inversions in the last-minute T+1 window—fares fell by 8.52 percent (₹10,665.50 to ₹9,757.00) and 5.67 percent (₹9,584.00 to ₹9,041.00) respectively—pointing toward spot-capacity additions or tactical distress-inventory clearance by operating carriers.

From a macroeconomic and monetary policy standpoint, the aggregated 1.35 percent rise in airfares indicates controlled, non-runaway service inflation within the civil aviation domain. The concentration of price gains in the 7-day to 30-day advance booking windows suggests resilient underlying travel demand, while last-minute yield softening helps buffer spot-market travelers against acute price shocks. The Reserve Bank of India and MoSPI will maintain active surveillance on these dynamic pricing trends, though immediate technical remediation of the raw data acquisition pipeline is requested to restore carrier-specific yield visibility ahead of the next inflation monitoring cycle.
